story.title: Six Killed in Krakow Shooting Linked to Far-Right Ideologies
story.summary: A mass shooting in Krakow left six people dead, including a British national, and injured at least 17 others. The 24-year-old Polish gunman, who reportedly had far-right affiliations, was critically injured during his arrest. Authorities have launched a terrorism investigation as they explore the suspect's extremist motives. Additionally, three bodies were discovered at the gunman's home, raising further concerns about the incident.

event_overview.title: About Krakow Shooting
event_overview.subject: Krakow Shooting
event_overview.summary: The Krakow shooting was a gun attack on 7 November 2026 in and around the Main Market Square in Krakow’s Old Town, Poland. Authorities reported six people killed and multiple people injured; the suspected attacker was shot and detained by police, while prosecutors opened a terrorism-related investigation.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The attack occurred shortly after 3 p.m. on 7 November 2026 near Sławkowska Street by Krakow’s Main Market Square (Rynek Główny).

facts.label: Casualties
facts.value: Krakow city authorities reported six deaths and 15 injuries in the shooting.

facts.label: Suspect and police response
facts.value: The city said the alleged attacker, identified by police as a Polish citizen, was shot and detained by officers after the incident.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: The National Prosecutor’s Office opened an investigation covering the killing of six people in Krakow and attempted killings of others, including police officers; prosecutors described the Krakow act as a terrorism-related crime.

facts.label: Official mourning
facts.value: Poland declared national mourning for 8–9 November 2026 in tribute to the victims; Krakow separately announced city mourning through 11 November.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected timeline follows the shooting, the initial official assessment of possible far-right motives, and mourning measures, but does not attempt to cover every investigative development, victim update, or related incident.

explore_lenses.label: Why is the terrorism designation significant?
explore_lenses.title: It elevates the case beyond a multiple-homicide inquiry
explore_lenses.summary: Prosecutors are treating the Kraków attack as a terrorist offense while investigating killings at the suspect's family home in the same case. That classification reflects the alleged intent and scale of the attack; it is not yet a court finding about motive or ideology.

claims.text: The National Prosecutor's Office said its inquiry covers the killing of six people in Kraków and attempted murder of many others, including police officers, with the act classified as a terrorist offense.
The investigation also covers the shooting deaths of three people in Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski; prosecutors say evidence so far indicates the same person committed both sets of killings.

Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the suspect held radical, ultra-nationalist views and was fascinated by far-right ideologies; this is an official assessment under investigation, not a judicially established motive.

explore_lenses.label: What do the linked home killings change?
explore_lenses.title: Investigators are examining a broader sequence of violence
explore_lenses.summary: The discovery of the suspect's parents and sister shifts the inquiry from an attack at one public site to an alleged series of connected killings. It also makes the timeline before the Kraków shooting central to determining planning, access to weapons and motive.

claims.text: Police identified the three people found dead at the family home as the suspect's father, mother and 21-year-old sister, with gunshot wounds preliminarily indicated.
The prosecutor's investigation formally combines the Kraków killings and the three deaths at the home, rather than treating them as unrelated incidents.

Officials reported that the suspect had a valid firearms license, while investigators were also examining the licensing issue; reporting said weapons and ammunition were found in his vehicle and that his father legally owned more than a dozen firearms.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the investigation?
explore_lenses.title: Charges await the suspect's medical condition
explore_lenses.summary: The suspect is hospitalized and under police guard, so investigators are continuing forensic and scene work before they can question him and seek formal pretrial measures. Public authorities have also moved from emergency response to mourning, victim support and security review.

claims.text: Prosecutor Tomasz Waszczuk said the suspect had not yet been formally detained because of his medical condition; prosecutors intend to conduct procedural steps, bring charges and decide on preventive measures when his health permits.

The Małopolska regional governor said the first police patrol reached the scene in under three minutes and exchanged fire with the attacker; more than 1,100 police officers and 62 firefighters were involved in the response.
Poland began national mourning on November 8 and 9 under a presidential decree, while Kraków and national officials continue coordinating medical, psychological and security responses.

story_report.summary: A shooting in Kraków killed six people, including a British national, and injured at least 17 others. Authorities identified the suspect as a 24-year-old Polish man with reported far-right affiliations and opened a terrorism investigation into the attack. Three additional bodies were found at the suspect’s family home, broadening the inquiry. Poland began two days of national mourning as officials continued medical, psychological and security responses.

sections.heading: Terrorism Inquiry Examines Motive
sections.body: The National Prosecutor’s Office said its investigation covers the killing of six people in Kraków and attempted murder of numerous others, including police officers, with the act classified as a terrorist offense. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the suspect held radical, ultra-nationalist views and was fascinated by far-right ideologies. That assessment remains under investigation rather than a judicially established motive.

sections.heading: Family Deaths and Firearms Inquiry
sections.body: Police identified the three people found dead at the family home as the suspect’s father, mother and 21-year-old sister; gunshot wounds were preliminarily indicated. Prosecutors have formally combined those deaths with the Kraków killings in one investigation. Officials said the suspect held a valid firearms licence, while investigators examine the licensing issue; weapons and ammunition were reportedly found in his vehicle, and his father legally owned more than a dozen firearms.

sections.heading: Suspect Remains Medically Unavailable
sections.body: Prosecutor Tomasz Waszczuk said the suspect had not yet been formally detained because of his medical condition. Prosecutors intend to carry out procedural steps, bring charges and consider preventive measures when his health permits. During the attack response, the first police patrol reached the scene in under three minutes and exchanged fire with the attacker; more than 1,100 police officers and 62 firefighters were involved.

unresolved.text: Authorities have not publicly detailed the evidence connecting ideology to the attack or said whether the suspect had any accomplices.
Public information does not establish the order of the family deaths and the Kraków attack, how any weapon was obtained, or the specific relationship between the incidents.
No timetable has been announced for charging or interviewing the suspect; early reports also differed on whether 15 or 17 people were injured.

related_stories.title: Paraguay's former president faces charges over Ueno Bank collapse
related_stories.summary: Santiago Peña, Paraguay's ousted president, has been charged with crimes related to the collapse of Ueno Bank, which left millions unable to access their funds. Prosecutors have ordered his arrest alongside former Central Bank chief Carlos Carvallo for alleged breach of trust and other offenses. Peña, who initially faced house arrest, has been moved to a military facility for safety amid ongoing protests from affected customers demanding access to their money.

related_stories.title: Kenyan Cult Leader Sentenced to 200 Years for Murder of 191 People
related_stories.summary: Paul Mackenzie, the leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect, has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult. The court found that Mackenzie incited his followers to starve themselves and their families in order to 'meet Jesus.' The sentence includes 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years for direct homicide.
